question: What is the unit of measurement for optical power of the lens?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Diopter**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The diopter (D) is the unit of measurement for the optical power of a lens or curved mirror.
 
• It is defined as the reciprocal of the focal length (f) measured in meters (i.e., D = 1/f).
 
• A lens with a focal length of 1 meter has an optical power of 1 diopter.
 
• Lenses with positive diopters are converging lenses, while those with negative diopters are diverging lenses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Optical Power:**

 
 
• Optical power, also known as lens power, is the degree to which a lens converges or diverges light.
 
• It is an important concept in optics and is essential in the design of optical systems such as glasses, cameras, and telescopes.
 
 
 
• **Focal Length:**
 
 
• The focal length of a lens is the distance from the lens at which parallel rays of light converge to a single point.
 
• It determines the magnifying power of the lens and is crucial in the formation of clear images.
 
 
 
• **Converging and Diverging Lenses:**
 
 
• Converging lenses (positive diopters) focus light to a point and are used in applications like magnifying glasses and corrective lenses for hyperopia (farsightedness).
 
• Diverging lenses (negative diopters) spread light outwards and are used in devices like peepholes and corrective lenses for myopia (nearsightedness).
